Reproducibility

How the fictional data were generated

A fixed-seed script creates fictional lodging attributes, prices, dates and data-quality defects. It defines the two-night total as two room nights plus cleaning, with tax on both. A separate fixture case illustrates joins and denominators.

Fixed seed: 41021. Read the complete generator and analysis code; inspect the saved results.

Known truth: The generator deliberately includes one duplicate and three incomplete records in the selected market. Those are known teaching facts, not discoveries about real hotels.

These are model assumptions and generated outcomes, not claims about a real population.

Stop 01 / 18

Start with a decision and a data passport

A colleague is comparing two-night stays across the fictional towns of Willow Bay, Cedar Reach and Juniper Vale. The decision is not “find the smallest number.” It is “choose an eligible, comparable offer within a budget.” Evidence must preserve what was observed, for whom, when and under which terms. In this lesson, all quotes and fixtures are newly generated teaching data, not market research.

Write a data passport before calculating: decision, target population, observation unit, fields, collection time, selection rules, provenance and known limits. Our target is the generated set of private-room hotel quotes for two specified arrival dates. We cannot infer availability, service quality or actual prices elsewhere.

  • Decision: shortlist comparable two-night hotel offers.
  • Observation: one lodging × arrival date quote, for one room.
  • Source: local simulation, seed 41021, prices in fictional currency units (CU).
  • Handoff: a comparable table, an audit trail and a bounded recommendation.

Pause and explain

Would “the cheapest hotel in Willow Bay” be supported by this exercise?

Compare your reasoning

No. We observe generated offers for specified dates and terms, not every real hotel or every possible stay. The defensible claim is cheapest among the eligible complete synthetic offers.

Stop 02 / 18

A row is a claim about an observation

The same lodging appears on two arrival dates. That is not automatically a duplicate: price can vary by date. A cross-section records entities at one time; a time series follows one entity through time; a panel follows multiple entities repeatedly. The unit determines which questions the table can answer and which fields must identify a row.

Three observation structures
StructureOne rowCandidate key
Cross-sectionOne lodging on one fixed datelodging_id
Time seriesOne lodging on each datearrival
PanelOne lodging × one datelodging_id + arrival

A quote is also not a booking or a guest. Counting quote rows does not count customers, purchases or occupied rooms. Changing the noun in the conclusion silently changes the estimand, the quantity the analysis is meant to describe.

Pause and explain

A lodging appears twice, on April 10 and April 17. Should one row be deleted?

Compare your reasoning

Not on that evidence. The composite key is lodging_id plus arrival. Two different dates represent two legitimate observations.

Stop 03 / 18

Check meaning, validity, reliability and coverage

A clean-looking table can still support the wrong decision. Meaning asks what the field denotes. Validity asks whether it measures the intended concept. Reliability asks whether repeated measurement is stable. Comparability asks whether the same definitions apply across rows. Coverage asks which members of the target population could appear. Selection asks why some actually appear.

A six-question trust check
QuestionRisk in a quote tableUseful response
MeaningNightly price mistaken for totalName currency, nights and inclusions
ValidityStar rating treated as service qualityState what the rating measures
ReliabilityQuotes change between retrievalsRecord retrieval time and terms
ComparabilityTax or room occupancy differsStandardize or separate offers
CoverageOnly one platform is observedLimit the population claim
SelectionOnly promoted listings are visibleDescribe the selection mechanism

These are design questions, not defects a prettier chart fixes. A reliable measure can still measure the wrong thing. A complete file can still omit the people or firms the decision concerns.

Pause and explain

Does a larger file repair a coverage gap?

Compare your reasoning

No. More observations from the same incomplete frame can reduce random error while preserving systematic exclusion.

Stop 04 / 18

Data collection changes who is visible

Administrative records cover activity a system records. Surveys cover those sampled and those who respond. Web listings cover what is published and retrievable. Experiments change an assignment mechanism but still need a recruitment frame. Benchmarking may compare organizations with different definitions. Each source has strengths, but none makes selection disappear.

Distinguish coverage from response. If only loyalty members receive a survey, nonmembers have no opportunity to appear. If every guest is invited but dissatisfied guests reply more often, response changes the observed mix. Increasing response among existing invitees does not add missing nonmembers.

Our simulation has deliberately complete knowledge of its generating process. That is a teaching advantage, not a claim about operational data. A real collection plan also needs lawful access, proportionate collection, privacy safeguards and documented permission for reuse. Do not store personal information merely because it is technically available.

Pause and explain

What is the first question before scraping a much larger list?

Compare your reasoning

Which population and fields are actually needed, whether access and reuse are permitted, and whether the new source changes the coverage or selection problem.

Stop 05 / 18

Define comparable quantities and variable types

Digits do not guarantee arithmetic is meaningful. A lodging identifier is nominal even if it contains numbers. A star rating is ordinal: five is ranked above four, but the difference need not equal the difference between three and two. A price has meaningful differences and ratios when currency and terms match. A date supports ordering and elapsed-time calculations, but not arbitrary ratios.

A compact data dictionary
FieldTypeDefensible operation
lodging_idNominal identifierMatch, count distinct values
ratingOrdinal categoryOrder, tabulate category shares
nightly_cuQuantitative ratio scaleCompare sums and ratios under common terms
refundableBinary categoryCount and calculate a defined share
arrivalDateOrder and calculate elapsed days
Two-night total = (2 × nightly price + cleaning fee) × (1 + tax rate)

Here tax is assumed to apply to both room and cleaning, and all offers use one room. These are explicit simulation assumptions. If a real jurisdiction taxes them differently, change the definition before computing.

Pause and explain

Can a hotel rated 4 be described as twice as good as a hotel rated 2?

Compare your reasoning

No. The rating is ordinal, not a ratio measure of quality. The numeric labels support order, not that ratio claim.

Stop 06 / 18

Verify identity before removing duplicates

The raw lab has 61 rows. One is an exact duplicate introduced to imitate an ingestion retry. Removing that exact repeated record leaves 60 distinct quote rows. The candidate key lodging_id + arrival is then unique. We do not delete all repeated lodging IDs, because the dates are part of the observation.

A duplicate key with different prices is a conflict, not an automatic invitation to keep the first row. Investigate whether the rows refer to different retrieval times, room types or refund terms. If a newer observation supersedes an older one, retain provenance and state the precedence rule. Entity resolution across misspelled names likewise needs recorded evidence and a reversible mapping.

Key check: number of distinct (lodging_id, arrival) pairs = number of rows

Uniqueness is necessary for this table, but not sufficient for truth. A unique row can still have the wrong unit, date or amount.

Pause and explain

Two rows share a key but one costs 80 CU and the other 95 CU. Is drop_duplicates a complete remedy?

Compare your reasoning

No. Exact de-duplication does not resolve conflicting values. Determine whether the observation definition needs another field or whether one value is an error, then document the decision.

Stop 07 / 18

Inspect values before narrowing the sample

Start with row count, field types, key uniqueness, missingness and plausible ranges. Preserve the original generated table, then create a working copy. The excerpt below deliberately includes problematic values and an exact repeated row. Missing and invalid values are different findings, even if both prevent a comparable total.

Synthetic raw excerpt, including known defects
LodgingArrivalKindRoomNightly CU
L0012030-04-17GuesthouseShared133.05
L0032030-04-10HotelPrivate77.78
L0052030-04-17HotelPrivatemissing
L0122030-04-10HotelPrivatemissing
L0182030-04-17HotelPrivate-15.00
L0032030-04-10HotelPrivate77.78

There are 2 initially missing prices and 1 nonpositive price. The lab flags the negative value, converts it to missing in the analysis copy, and does not guess a replacement. A zero might be meaningful in another domain, so this is a price-specific validation rule rather than a universal cleaning habit.

Pause and explain

Why keep the raw table after making corrections?

Compare your reasoning

It separates what arrived from what the analyst changed. A colleague can audit each rule, reproduce the analysis and revise a rule without reconstructing lost information.

Stop 08 / 18

A filter changes the population

We keep exact kind = Hotel and room = Private rows after removing the known duplicate. That leaves 40 quote rows. Of these, 3 cannot produce a valid total, leaving 37 complete comparable quotes. We report both the eligibility filter and the completeness exclusion.

Synthetic preparation funnel — chart data
GroupQuote rows
Raw61
Distinct60
In scope40
Complete37

Exact matching is deliberate: a Guesthouse is not silently recoded as a Hotel. Conversely, genuine spelling variants would require a documented normalization rule. This filter does not fix platform coverage, measurement validity or the fact that two arrival dates are a limited window.

Pause and explain

Does the final row count prove the missing quotes are irrelevant?

Compare your reasoning

No. If missingness depends on price or lodging type, the complete-case summary can shift. Report the missingness and investigate its cause before generalizing.

Stop 09 / 18

Calculate a comparable offer, then qualify the choice

The following offers are sorted by the same two-night total, with tax and cleaning handled consistently. Sorting by nightly price alone can reverse a comparison when fixed fees differ. Refundability and walking distance remain separate decision attributes; compressing them into a score requires explicit weights.

Six lowest eligible complete synthetic offers
LodgingTownArrivalNightly CUCleaning CUTotal CURefundable
L020Cedar Reach2030-04-1751.7512.00124.74Yes
L020Cedar Reach2030-04-1070.0212.00164.20Yes
L002Cedar Reach2030-04-1074.8812.00174.70Yes
L024Juniper Vale2030-04-1069.9024.00176.90Yes
L025Willow Bay2030-04-1082.890.00179.04No
L010Willow Bay2030-04-1783.500.00180.36Yes

A ranking is conditional on the chosen outcome and eligibility rules. The cheapest complete observation does not establish best service, best overall value or future availability. A defensible shortlist names the price measure and leaves judgment about other attributes visible.

Pause and explain

If the cheapest offer is nonrefundable, must it be selected?

Compare your reasoning

No. The total answers a cost question. Flexibility is another criterion, and its value depends on the traveler’s needs. Apply an explicit constraint or trade-off instead of pretending price captures everything.

Stop 10 / 18

Change layout without changing meaning

A second miniature case tracks fictional service requests by town and quarter. In wide form, quarters occupy columns. In long form, quarter becomes a variable and requests becomes the value. A reshape changes representation, not the underlying observation unit: one town-quarter remains one observation.

Synthetic service requests, wide layout
TownQ1Q2Q3
Willow Bay1198072.0
Cedar Reach106106122.0
Juniper Vale106106missing

Willow Bay, Q2 equals 80 requests in both layouts. Juniper Vale, Q3 is unrecorded. It is not zero requests. A total over observed quarters answers a different question from a full-year total, so a skip-missing default must not be interpreted as complete coverage.

Pause and explain

What must remain attached to a value after reshaping?

Compare your reasoning

Its identifying fields, unit and missingness status. The value alone is not enough: town and quarter tell us which observation it describes.

Stop 11 / 18

Melt, pivot and join are different operations

Melt collects selected value columns into a variable/value pair. Pivot spreads a variable into columns and requires one value per output cell. A join attaches fields using matching keys. These operations are easy to confuse because each changes the visible table, but they preserve different relationships.

Synthetic service requests after melt
TownQuarterRequests
Willow BayQ1119.0
Cedar ReachQ1106.0
Juniper ValeQ1106.0
Willow BayQ280.0
Cedar ReachQ2106.0
Juniper ValeQ2106.0
Willow BayQ372.0
Cedar ReachQ3122.0
Juniper ValeQ3missing

Before pivoting, verify town + quarter uniqueness. If two source rows map to one cell, an aggregation such as mean or sum is a substantive decision, not a neutral reshape. A pivot table may silently aggregate where a strict pivot would correctly expose a conflict.

Pause and explain

Two records map to Willow Bay, Q2. Why not average them automatically?

Compare your reasoning

They may be duplicates, different service categories or revised observations. Averaging could erase the actual observation definition. Resolve the key or justify a specific aggregation first.

Stop 12 / 18

A join can multiply the evidence

Each quote needs one walking-distance attribute from a lodging dimension. The safe many-to-one join keeps 37 rows and verifies every key matched. Deliberately duplicating one dimension key creates 39 rows in the unsafe join. A duplicated quote then receives extra weight in later averages.

Join cardinality is part of the analysis
RelationshipExpected key patternTypical safeguard
One-to-oneBoth sides uniqueValidate both keys
Many-to-oneRepeated left keys, unique right keysValidate right key and row-count stability
Many-to-manyBoth sides repeatExplain intended combinations or redesign keys

Record unmatched keys as well as row growth. An inner join can shrink the sample by dropping unmatched observations; a left join preserves them but may introduce missing attributes. Validate cardinality, compare row counts and inspect the match indicator before calculating.

Pause and explain

A join succeeds without an error. Does that prove it is correct?

Compare your reasoning

No. Unless cardinality and coverage were explicitly checked, a syntactically valid join may duplicate or drop observations and change the analysis population.

Stop 13 / 18

An event can produce multiple observations

The next case contains 24 fictional fixtures among Aster, Bracken, Clover and Dahlia. A fixture is one event, but team performance needs one observation per team per fixture. Transforming each event into home-team and away-team records gives 48 team-game rows.

Two freshly simulated fixtures
DateHomeAwayHome goalsAway goals
2030-01-05AsterBracken02
2030-01-05CloverDahlia21
Team points = 3 for a win; 1 for a draw; 0 for a loss

The two rows from a fixture are linked: one team’s win implies the other team’s loss. This dependence matters for later inference even though row expansion is correct for descriptive grouping. Distinguish the reporting unit from the independent unit.

Pause and explain

Does expanding 24 events to 48 team rows create 48 independent games?

Compare your reasoning

No. It creates two perspectives on each event, not twice as much independent evidence. Both the event ID and team ID should be retained.

Stop 14 / 18

Assign time-varying attributes with date boundaries

Each fictional team changes manager on February 16. Joining by team alone gives 96 candidate rows because every game matches both managers. We retain the match whose date falls inside its tenure. A half-open interval includes the start and excludes the end: start ≤ date < end.

A synthetic boundary-date assignment
FixtureDateTeamAssigned managerPoints
F112030-02-09AsterAster North0
F132030-02-16AsterAster South3

The new manager owns February 16; the previous tenure ends immediately before it. Verify that each team-game has exactly one match. Zero matches signal a gap. Multiple matches signal overlapping tenures or a duplicate definition. Both require investigation before a summary is credible.

Pause and explain

If both tenures include their end date, what goes wrong on February 16?

Compare your reasoning

The boundary game can match both managers and be counted twice. A consistent half-open interval avoids that ambiguity.

Stop 15 / 18

The group and denominator define the result

Group by team and manager together, then calculate games, observed point values, total points and points per game. The distinction between row count and nonmissing count is important: a mean can silently ignore missing outcomes while a game count includes them. Our generated outcome fields are complete, and the lab checks that explicitly.

Synthetic team-manager summaries
TeamManagerGamesObservedTotal pointsPoints/game
BrackenBracken North66183.000
DahliaDahlia South66122.000
AsterAster South6691.500
BrackenBracken South6691.500
CloverClover North6691.500
DahliaDahlia North6691.500
CloverClover South6661.000
AsterAster North6600.000
Points per game = total recorded points / games with recorded points

When all outcomes are complete, that denominator equals games played. Otherwise report the gap and avoid labeling a partial-outcome average as a complete performance rate. An aggregation discards within-group detail, so retain the prepared event table for audit.

Pause and explain

A group has 10 game rows but only 8 recorded point values. What does its default mean use?

Compare your reasoning

Usually the 8 nonmissing values. Dividing their sum by 10 instead answers a different question and implicitly treats missing outcomes as zero. Investigate and disclose the gap.

Stop 16 / 18

Weight rates by their actual exposure

Averaging group averages gives each group equal influence. Pooling observations weights each group by its number of observations. Neither is automatically wrong; they answer different questions. Name whether the target is the average group or the average observation.

An explicitly authored synthetic denominator example
GroupGamesPointsPoints/game
Short tenure263
Long tenure881
Pooled rate = (6 + 8) / (2 + 8) = 1.40; equal-group mean = (3 + 1) / 2 = 2.00
Mean comparable two-night total by fictional town — chart data
GroupCU
Cedar Reach258.413
Juniper Vale256.21
Willow Bay239.063

The lodging chart is descriptive of complete in-scope quote rows. Town means can also reflect room mix, dates and selection. A group comparison is not an explanation of why the groups differ.

Pause and explain

Which rate describes a randomly selected game from the ten-game toy dataset?

Compare your reasoning

The pooled rate, 1.40 points per game. The equal-group average describes selecting a tenure uniformly and then using its average.

Stop 17 / 18

A ranking is a conditional description

In this simulation, the highest team-manager average is Bracken North with 3.000 points per game across 6 games. The illustration uses an eligibility threshold of at least six games, stated before ranking. All qualifying groups remain visible, including ties.

Eligibility controls which comparisons are reported; it does not create causal comparability. Manager assignments, team quality, opponents, injuries and timing can differ. A short-tenure threshold also is not a reliable label for caretaker status. Do not infer a job category from a duration filter alone.

  • Supported: this group has the highest observed rate among eligible groups in this generated schedule.
  • Unsupported: this manager caused the highest performance or would improve every team.
  • Useful next step: inspect schedule balance, uncertainty and the assignment process before a consequential decision.

Pause and explain

Why is “best manager” stronger than the calculation supports?

Compare your reasoning

The calculation ranks observed outcomes under specific teams and schedules. It does not isolate managerial contribution from the other causes of those outcomes.

Stop 18 / 18

Leave an audit trail and a bounded recommendation

Use a repeatable sequence: detect, decide, correct and document. Checks should cover identity, scope, values and relationships. Every correction should have a reason, a reversible transformation and a measurable consequence such as rows affected. Missingness is an investigation prompt, not an automatic deletion instruction.

A defensible handoff checklist
Audit fieldWhat this lab records
IdentityComposite quote key; fixture + team key
ScopePrivate-room Hotel quotes on two arrival dates
ValuesMissing prices, nonpositive-price flag, explicit tax formula
RelationshipsMany-to-one lodging join; date-aware manager assignment
ReproductionSeed 41021, standalone code, calculated JSON and notebook
LimitSynthetic exercise, no evidence about actual markets or managers

Management handoff: “I compared 37 complete synthetic quotes under a common two-night price definition. I removed one known ingestion duplicate, flagged invalid prices and verified key-safe joins. The shortlist is conditional on eligibility and completeness. Review refundability and trip requirements before selecting an offer.”

Next, Lesson 2 asks what the remaining observations look like. Distributional analysis begins only after the observation, population and preparation choices are defensible.

Pause and explain

What should a colleague be able to do with the handoff?

Compare your reasoning

Rebuild the result from the standalone lab, explain every denominator and exclusion, identify its main limitation, and understand the action the evidence can support.
